macro_blurb: Geopolitics is front and center after the US military confirmed two American service members killed and one missing in Jordan amid the escalating Iran conflict, with Tehran calling off an interim peace deal and threatening retaliation — a setup that typically pressures European and US risk assets while supporting energy and defense-linked names. On the US corporate side, headlines flag a strong start to earnings season being overshadowed by an ongoing AI rotation, and a Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce recall across 27 states adds a small overhang for the packaged foods and grocery segment. Wall Street is also recalibrating to the Fed's new communication style ("WarshGPT" era), keeping rate-path interpretation in focus. In Germany, political noise around Spahn's resignation, the AfD's Saxony-Anhalt campaign kickoff and Merz's succession plans adds a domestic backdrop for DAX participants.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a pure US value-and-yield print, with zero European names in the top 10 despite 969 tickers screened. Composition tilts hard: average Value percentile sits at 88.6 and Yield at 83.7, while Quality lags at 57.7 — the model is paying for cheapness and cash, not for balance-sheet strength. Sector distribution is defensive-cyclical barbell: Consumer Defensive, Utilities and Basic Materials each contribute two picks, with Technology represented only by HPQ. Six of ten names carry dividend yields above 4%, and four trade below 11x trailing earnings.

The clearest thread runs through the rate-sensitive income complex: Eversource (ES) and Edison (EIX) both surface at top-decile Value and Yield inside Utilities, with EIX at 8.4x earnings and ES at 16x, riding "WarshGPT"-era rate-path uncertainty as a re-rating catalyst — but both carry debt/equity above 180. A second thread is deep-value consumer cash-return: MO (5.71% yield), KHC (6.18% yield, 0.73 P/B) and HPQ (15.2% FCF yield) all screen top-decile on Yield with Quality either missing or negative. The Jordan escalation and Iran retaliation risk sit awkwardly against this: no Energy names cleared the screen.

The outlier is CNC — 73% three-month return, 20.9% FCF yield, but -26% ROE. It fits nothing except the Value factor at 100th percentile. Conspicuous absences: Energy, Industrials, Real Estate and Communication Services returned nothing, and only one Tech name made it despite the AI-rotation headlines. Watch the Iran retaliation path and the Fed's next communication signal — either could reprice the utilities pair and the tobacco/packaged-foods bid inside two weeks.
